candidates.buyer: Officers of registered societies under the Societies Act Cap 108: church and community associations, clubs, welfare, burial, self-help and alumni groups; plus bookkeepers who serve them
candidates.evidence: People Daily and Standard (May 2026) report the AG/Registrar notice; Kenya Law holds the Societies Rules 1968, amended 2021 (LN 259/2021). URLs: https://peopledaily.digital/news/govt-issues-60-day-compliance-window-for-registered-societies-to-file-annual-returns/amp ; https://www.standardmedia.co.ke/crime-and-justice/article/2001547890/societies-risk-suspension-if-they-fail-to-file-annual-returns-within-60-days ; https://new.kenyalaw.org/akn/ke/act/ln/1968/62 ; https://statelaw.go.ke/registrar-general-division/registration-of-societies
candidates.existing: Competitor search (societies annual return Form I / app / eCitizen) found no compliance software for societies; the only tools found were company annual-return guides. Online filing of Form I for societies is unconfirmed.
candidates.known_note: K04 covers co-operatives and non-deposit SACCOs under the Commissioner for Co-operatives. Societies are a different buyer and a different registrar.
candidates.name: Societies annual-return (Form I) and officer-register pack for small registered societies, churches and welfare groups
candidates.trigger: Societies Act s.30(1) and Rule 13 Societies Rules 1968: annual return on Form I by 31 March each year, signed by 3 officers. Registrar notice of 15 May 2026 gave a 60-day window before show-cause, suspension or cancellation (s.12(1)(e)).
candidates.unchecked: Number of active societies; whether the Registrar has an online portal and what the compliance rate is; willingness to pay (low-margin volunteer officers); whether Form I filing is manual only; the status of the new Societies law or rules after the 60-day window; fee per return.

candidates.buyer: Small NGOs and CBOs registered under the PBO Act 2013 (PBORA, replacing the NGO Coordination Board)
candidates.existing: Competitor search specific to PBO/PBORA was not run (budget cap). The societies search found no compliance software. Existing NGO consultancies and accounting firms likely serve this: unverified.
candidates.known_note: Adjacent to K04 in being a registry-annual-return duty on non-profit bodies, but a different regulator and buyer.
candidates.name: PBO annual report and re-registration pack for small public benefit organisations (CBOs, small charities)
candidates.trigger: PBO Act in force May 2024; old NGOs had to re-register and align by 13 May 2026; every PBO must file annual reports on prescribed forms; 2025 reports for Dec year-end extended to 9 July 2026 after eCitizen payment problems. 2026 PBO Regulations.
candidates.unchecked: Competitor search (PBORA annual report software, consultants); number of PBOs; whether the 13 May 2026 re-registration deadline was extended again; PBORA fee levels; whether NGOs already use grant-management tools.

candidates.buyer: Small workplaces and plant owners (factories, workshops, garages, hotels with lifts or boilers, LPG users) and small approved OSH advisers, auditors and plant examiners who file for them
candidates.category: 12. Lift, boiler and pressure-equipment owners and inspectors
candidates.evidence: https://doshmis.go.ke/services/plant-inspection ; https://new.kenyalaw.org/akn/ke/act/ln/2022/50/eng@2022-03-29 ; https://www.doshmis.go.ke/faqs ; DOSHS user guide of 22 Sept 2025 at https://doshmis.go.ke/public/user_guides/DOSHS User Guide (Final draft OSH fees 22nd September 2025).pdf
candidates.existing: Competitor search (OSH audit software Kenya DOSHMIS) found no DOSHS-endorsed audit app. Found consultancies (Strategic SHE Ltd, Arinite) that mention commercial HSE platforms. DOSHMIS itself is the free state portal for registration.
candidates.name: Workplace registration, plant certificate and audit tracker for small OSH-registered workplaces and approved examiners (lifts, boilers, air receivers, LPG cylinders)
candidates.trigger: OSH Act 2007: annual workplace registration via DOSHMIS (forms DOSHS 21A/21B/23, self-assessment), plant registration on DOSHS 20 (about KSh 1,000 per lift, boiler, crane or large cylinder in a September 2025 draft fee guide), periodic thorough examination by approved persons, and safety and fire audits (KSh 2,000 submission fee per the draft guide). OSH Fees Regulations LN 50/2022.
candidates.unchecked: Exact examination intervals per plant type; true workplace-registration fee (KSh 2,000 vs 5,000 conflict); count of approved examiners and auditors; whether DOSHMIS already sends renewal reminders; whether fire-safety certification sits with the county, not DOSHS; actual enforcement intensity.

candidates.buyer: Independent driving schools and instructors across Kenya (Kenya Driving Schools Association members)
candidates.category: 20. Small licensed premises with inspections: driving schools
candidates.existing: Competitor search (driving school management software Kenya NTSA) found no vendor. Regulatory churn is a risk: the 2020 Rules were halted by a court after a Kenya Driving Schools Association petition.
candidates.name: Driving school operations and NTSA compliance pack (student admissions, attendance, instructor ratio, vehicle and insurance records)
candidates.trigger: NTSA notice of 14 April 2026: all driving schools must register via eCitizen with inspection (Traffic Act penalty up to KSh 20,000 or at least 6 months). Traffic (Driving Schools, Driving Instructors and Driving Licences) Rules 2018; instructor eligibility rules 2026. Business Daily report of a new curriculum from October (year not shown) requiring lessons at licensed schools.
candidates.unchecked: Number of licensed schools; whether the NTSA portal for schools is functional; October curriculum year and whether it passed; whether a recurring report to NTSA exists (as opposed to one-off registration); price tolerance of small schools; generic school-management competitors.

candidates.buyer: Small manufacturers, importers and re-brand/private-label sellers who have to join NEMA's EPR system or a producer responsibility organisation
candidates.category: 11. Septic, sanitation and waste haulers (adjacent: waste regime)
candidates.existing: Competitor search (EPR compliance software Kenya NEMA) found no EPR software. PROs such as KEPRO and law firms advise. The buyer is not a quiet family business, and producers are likely larger.
candidates.name: EPR registration, volume register and annual report pack for small importers and manufacturers
candidates.trigger: Sustainable Waste Management (Extended Producer Responsibility) Regulations 2024, LN 176/2024, in force 4 Nov 2024: register with NEMA, annual licence, 4-year EPR plan, volume-based fees, EPR certificate (KES 150 per item) for clearance of listed imports. Full enforcement announced Dec 2025 after court orders lifted.
candidates.unchecked: Whether small firms have a de minimis threshold; fee schedule; which exact tasks recur (annual returns); PRO coverage; whether NEMA runs a free portal; relevance to this study's 'quiet small business' focus.

candidates.buyer: Owners and operators of commercial vehicles, including small truck and bus fleets
candidates.category: 18. Transport operators: small trucking and bus fleets
candidates.existing: Competitor search (fleet/telematics compliance software Kenya NTSA) found no named vendor; telematics and fleet-tracking vendors almost certainly exist (unverified). Regulation status and size thresholds unconfirmed.
candidates.known_note: K13 is matatu SACCOs (rejected, crowded). This is goods-vehicle and bus operators under a different 2026 rule.
candidates.name: Commercial-vehicle operator record pack (service records, driver hours, fatal-accident report) for small trucking and bus operators
candidates.trigger: National Transport and Safety (Operation of Commercial Vehicles) Regulations 2026 (reported as expected enactment around 1 July 2026): service records kept 2 years, qualified drivers, driving-hour limits, fatal-accident report within 20 hours, NTSA safety audits, telematics and underride protection (Reg. 9). NTSA later said enforcement of 9(d) telematics and 9(h) will be communicated later.
candidates.unchecked: Whether the regulation was gazetted; vehicle-size thresholds (above 3,048 kg tare reported); who actually inspects records; competition from fleet-tracking vendors; paused inspection and telematics rules.

candidates.buyer: Boda boda Saccos and associations, riders
candidates.existing: No boda-specific competitor search run. K13 reports SaccoWorks, MatatuOS and Simple Fare in the matatu space; coverage of boda Saccos is unverified.
candidates.known_note: Same sector family as K13, but boda Saccos and county permit regime; rider fragmentation and low willingness to pay.
candidates.name: Boda boda Sacco and permit management (Nairobi Motorcycle Taxi Permit Regulations 2025; Sacco registration with NTSA and county)
candidates.trigger: Nairobi City County (Motorcycle Taxi (Boda Boda) Permit) Regulations 2025; April 2026 mandatory rider registration under Saccos or companies, annual permits, 67-member enforcement unit; NTSA National Road Safety Action Plan 2024-2028 reported to require Saccos of at least 100 members.
candidates.unchecked: Competitor search; whether the 100-member Sacco rule is law; number of Nairobi permit-holders; whether the county runs its own portal.

candidates.buyer: Community water projects, kiosk operators, private suppliers and tanker/borehole sellers
candidates.evidence: https://www.capitalfm.co.ke/news/?p=768471 ; https://www.kenyanews.go.ke/?p=145550 ; https://test.capitalfm.africa/wasreb-to-shut-unregistered-water-kiosks-after-april-28/ ; https://wasreb.go.ke/licensing-tariff/ . The Kenya Times page was blocked (403).
candidates.existing: No competitor search run. The registration was free and online only, a state tool. K12 (WRA app and smart meters) covers abstraction, not WASREB service provision.
candidates.known_note: K12 concerns WRA abstraction permits. This is the WASREB service-provision licence for a different set of operators.
candidates.name: WASREB small-scale water provider register and returns (kiosks, tankers, community projects)
candidates.trigger: Water Act 2016 s.85 (no water services without a WASREB licence); WASREB ordered small-scale providers to register online by 28 April 2025; Water Services Regulations 2025; WASREB rural guideline reportedly requires community institutions to register as Water User Associations.
candidates.unchecked: Whether a 2026 deadline or periodic data return exists; fees; operator count; competitor search; official WASREB data-collection page was not read.

candidates.name: Livestock trader and slaughter traceability records (ANITRAC Animal Identification and Traceability Bill 2026)
candidates.trigger: Draft Animal Identification and Traceability Bill 2026: compulsory animal registration, RFID tags, transfer-of-ownership records and transaction fees at transfer points (slaughter, export); animals presented to slaughterhouses must bear identification devices. Pilot in 6 counties. County sale-yard laws already require licensed traders and movement permits.
candidates.unchecked: Bill text (operative provisions, trader duties, fees); whether tabled or passed; whether a mobile/USSD interface for traders is supplied by the state.

candidates.trigger: NEA rules: KSh 500,000 initial registration, renewal every 2 years, in-person vetting; approval before sending workers abroad; Labour Migration and Management (No. 2) Bill 2024 under review (June 2026); 400 agencies banned.
candidates.unchecked: What returns agencies must file; whether NEA has its own system; size of the licensed market; competitor search.

coverage.category: 1. Household employers: domestic workers, live-in carers, nannies
coverage.found: Two searches found no household-specific rule. Only generic employer duties: NSSF 6%+6% (upper earnings limit KES 108,000 from Feb 2026), SHIF 2.75% employee-only, Housing Levy 1.5%+1.5%, remittance by the 9th. A 2013 NSSF domestic-worker drive is the only domestic-specific item (old). General payroll is rejected as K10, so nothing new unless a household-specific registration rule is found. Unchecked: whether KRA/NSSF/SHA have a household-employer channel.

coverage.category: 2. Scrap-metal dealers
coverage.found: Nothing new beyond K05. Not re-checked, per the contract.

coverage.category: 3. Second-hand dealers and pawnbrokers
coverage.found: Kenya has the Pawnbrokers Act (Cap. 529): annual licence and books kept per First Schedule. No Kenyan second-hand-goods register law found (South African results ignored). Tiny, thinly documented niche. Statutory text not read.

coverage.category: 4. Gold and jewellery buyers
coverage.found: Mining Act Cap 306 ss.159-175 and Mining (Dealings in Minerals) Regulations LN 88/2017, amended by LN 41 of 2024. Mineral Dealer (Jewellery) licence reported at KSh 20,000 a year (forms DJL-1/DJL-2); record-keeping duty at s.163. Returns schedule and 2025-26 changes not found. Not verified at source.

coverage.category: 5. Used car parts and vehicle dismantlers
coverage.found: No Kenyan dismantler or end-of-life-vehicle licensing rule found. Only the draft National Automotive Industry Development Bill 2025 (about 30,000 written-off vehicles on the NTSA database to be decommissioned) and vague government plans. Nothing buildable yet; revisit if the bill passes.

coverage.category: 6. Livestock traders, markets and animal transport
coverage.found: County sale-yard laws (Mandera, Kilifi, Kakamega bill 2024) require licensed traders, inspection and movement permits. National Animal Identification and Traceability (ANITRAC) Bill 2026 is still a draft (validation meeting 15 July 2026). Pilot in 6 counties. No fee amounts or trader duties confirmed. Candidate logged as unverified.

coverage.category: 7. Small abattoirs and butchers
coverage.found: Meat Control Act Cap 356 plus county abattoir and meat-inspector rules. Enforcement is uneven, and Oct 2025 warnings of inspector-butcher collusion. ANITRAC would barcode carcasses at slaughter, but is only a draft. No national recurring filing found. Folded into the ANITRAC candidate.

coverage.category: 8. Beekeepers
coverage.found: Livestock (Bee industry) Regulations 2023 (per KALRO compendium) cover registration and hive rules; the Livestock Bill fines (KES 500,000) were only proposed. Honey processors need KEBS KS 2949 and a county certificate. Legal status unconfirmed. Weak candidate.

coverage.category: 9. Veterinary practices and veterinary medicine sellers
coverage.found: Veterinary Surgeons and Para-Professionals Act 2011: KVB annual licence needing CPD (14 points for para-professionals, Form 27 by 30 Nov, per a secondary source). VMD registers products. Agrovet multi-regulator angle is K11 (rejected). A CPD and licence tracker is a thin idea. Nothing new beyond K11.

coverage.category: 10. Well drillers and water abstraction
coverage.found: Nothing new beyond K12 (rejected, WRA app). Not re-checked.

coverage.category: 11. Septic, sanitation and waste haulers
coverage.found: Search found no waste-transporter licensing text. Found EPR Regulations 2024 (LN 176/2024): all producers and importers must register with NEMA, hold an annual licence, file a 4-year plan, pay volume-based fees, and importers need an EPR certificate (KES 150 per item). Enforcement fully resumed Dec 2025. This hits small importers and manufacturers, logged as an adjacent candidate.

coverage.category: 12. Lift, boiler and pressure-equipment owners and inspectors
coverage.found: OSH Act 2007: annual workplace registration via DOSHMIS (forms DOSHS 21A/21B/23; fee reported as KSh 2,000 in the 2022 regulations and KSh 5,000 on the DOSHMIS FAQ, so unreconciled). Plant (lifts, boilers, air receivers, cylinders) registration on DOSHS 20 with periodic thorough examination by approved plant examiners. Safety and fire audits by approved auditors. No DOSHS-endorsed audit software found.

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: WASREB ordered small-scale providers (community projects, kiosks, tankers, private suppliers) to register online by 28 April 2025 (Water Act 2016 s.85; Water Services Regulations 2025). No 2026 deadline found; the rural guideline is only a secondary source. Fetch of the Kenya Times page was blocked (403). Weak candidate.

coverage.category: 14. Pesticide and fertiliser dealers and applicators
coverage.found: Nothing new beyond K11 (rejected). Not re-checked.

coverage.category: 15. Labour contractors and recruitment agencies
coverage.found: NEA private employment agencies: new regulations raised initial registration to KSh 500,000, renewal to 2 years, and agencies must appear before a vetting committee. 932 registered but only 531 with valid licences (earlier count); 400 banned. Labour Migration and Management Bill (No. 2) 2024 under review (20 June 2026). Per-agency returns not found. Weak candidate.

coverage.category: 16. Cemeteries, burial societies and funeral services
coverage.found: Private funeral homes are licensed by KMPDC (registration KSh 15,000 plus licence KSh 20,000 per a community wiki; renewal online; figures unverified). Burial permits under the Births and Deaths Registration Act; April 2026 Kericho prosecution for burying 33 bodies without permits. No county cemetery regime found. Small buyer pool.

coverage.category: 17. Community and religious bodies: associations, charities, halal and kosher supervision
coverage.found: Strong finding. Societies Act s.30(1) and Rule 13 require an annual return on Form I by 31 March, signed by 3 officers. The Registrar's notice of 15 May 2026 gave a 60-day window before show-cause, suspension or cancellation. Churches, clubs and welfare groups are covered. No compliance app found, and online filing for societies unconfirmed. Separately, the PBO Act regime (PBORA) required re-registration by 13 May 2026 and annual reports (2025 reports extended to 9 July 2026). Halal and kosher supervision: not searched.

coverage.category: 18. Transport operators: minibus, taxi, moto-taxi, small trucking and bus fleets
coverage.found: Boda boda: Nairobi Motorcycle Taxi Permit Regulations 2025 and April 2026 mandatory registration under Saccos or companies, annual permits, NTSA plans for 100-member Saccos (national status unclear). National Transport and Safety (Operation of Commercial Vehicles) Regulations 2026: 2-year service records, fatal-accident report within 20 hours, safety audits; telematics enforcement paused by NTSA (Reg. 9(d),(h)). Mandatory vehicle inspection enforcement suspended; DG says centres by June 2027. Matatu Saccos remain K13 (rejected).

coverage.category: 19. Market traders, street vendors, money changers
coverage.found: County Single Business Permits are fragmented by county (Nairobi unified permit from Jan 2024; Nakuru unified permit; Kisumu estimates about 30% of SBP revenue lost to fake permits). No national recurring filing; the buyer is the county. Forex bureaus: CBK directory updated April 2026, licences under CBK and AML reporting to the FRC; the pool is small and licence-heavy. No concrete candidate.

coverage.category: 20. Small licensed premises with inspections: tattoo studios, driving schools, childminders and nurseries, small food producers, hunting outfitters
coverage.found: Driving schools: NTSA notice of 14 April 2026 requires all driving schools to register (eCitizen, inspection, penalty up to KSh 20,000 or at least 6 months); instructor rules (4 years' experience, good conduct, medical); a report of a driving curriculum starting October (year unconfirmed); records NTSA has asked for in past vetting (admissions, attendance, instructor ratio, vehicles, insurance). Childcare: governed by the ECDE Act 2021 and county ECD regulations (Kisumu 2026); Children Act 2022 regulations still pending. Food: county food-handler medical certificates and KEBS for processed foods, both fragmented. Tattoo studios and hunting outfitters: not searched, no signal.
